predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor 'Abbasid Caliphate': Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Saj 'was appointed as its ruler in 889 or 890' (Azerbaijan).

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Sallarid dynasty'; the Sajid page dates the Sallarid expansion 'into Azerbaijan in 941', twelve years after the Sajid dynasty ended in 929, so 930-940 is unaccounted for.

capitals.name: Maragha
capitals.note: Infobox 'Maragha (889-901)'; Yusuf demolished its walls in 901.

capitals.name: Ardabil
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ardabil (901-929)'; the page adds that the Sajids 'usually resided in Barda' (Arran).

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Saj
rulers.note: A Bosworth citation dates his appointment c. 892 against the text's 889 or 890.

rulers.name: Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj
rulers.note: Captured and imprisoned in Baghdad in 919, released 922.

rulers.name: Yusuf ibn Abi'l-Saj (restored)
rulers.note: Captured by the Qarmatians after Kufa and killed in 928.

rulers.name: Fath ibn Muhammad (Abu'l-Musafir al-Fath)
rulers.note: Nephew of Yusuf; the dynasty ends in 929.

correction.text: the 898-910 shape used for 889-897: Azerbaijan around Maragha with the Araxes lands to Dvin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 889-897, which Cliopatria lacks (its row starts 898, the year the coins are first struck in Muhammad's name, 898-900). Infobox 'Established: 889'; Muhammad 'was appointed as its ruler in 889 or 890', the capital was Maragha, and he 'succeeded in incorporating much of the South Caucasus into the Sajid state' with a western border at 'Ani and Dabil (Dvin)'. The page does not date the Caucasian conquests inside his reign, so the 898 shape is used as a proxy for the whole of 889-897.

57.9 thousand km2, bbox 44.5-49.2E, 36.9-42.0N: Azerbaijan from Maragha and Ardabil with the Araxes valley to Dvin. The page gives no area and no boundary, so no comparison; the shape holds 898-910 (Yusuf's accession 901 and his 909 investiture change no border).

58.2 thousand km2 for 911-925. Right for 911-916. The Yusuf page: 'After Ibn al-Furat regained the vizierate in 917, Yusuf conquered Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray from the Samanids' and in 924 'conquered Ray from its governor'; the bounding box stops at 36.9N and misses all four. The 914 Georgian campaign (Tiflis as his base) is not a held conquest and is not drawn.

correction.text: the 911 shape plus Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 917-928: the 911 shape plus Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray. Yusuf was imprisoned in Baghdad 919-922 (Subuk held Azerbaijan) and 'invested with the governorship of Azerbaijan' in 922 'along with the provinces taken from the Samanids'; Ray was reconquered in 924.

correction.text: the 926 shape plus Zanjan-Qazvin-Ray, ending 929 rather than 935

keyframe_review.note: Holds 926-929, with the Zanjan-Ray extension of sajid-dynasty_917 to Yusuf's death in 928. The Sajid page ends the dynasty in 929 ('was poisoned in Ardabil by one of his slaves, which ended the Sajid dynasty'); Cliopatria runs to 935 and the page does not say who held Azerbaijan in 930-940 (Sallarid expansion 'in 941').

ledger.note: 889: Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Saj takes up the governorship of Azerbaijan at Maragha. Infobox 'Established: 889', 'Capital: Maragha (889-901)'; he 'was appointed as its ruler in 889 or 890'. 'At the end of the ninth century (898-900)' coins were struck in his name and he 'was able to form a virtually independent state'.

901: Yusuf overthrows his nephew and moves the capital to Ardabil. 'Yusuf came to power in 901 by overthrowing his nephew'; he 'demolished the walls of Maragha and moved the capital to Ardabil' (Sajid page; its infobox 'Capital: Maragha (889–901) Ardabil (901–929)' gives the year; source set to the Sajid page by the me-08-b reviewer).

909: Yusuf takes Nakhichevan and shares Siunikh. 'In 909 Yusuf took Nakhichevan and, together with Gagik, gained control of Siunikh'; the same year the peace of 908-909 let the caliph invest him 'with the governments of Azerbaijan and Armenia'.
c. 909: the Shirvanshah becomes dependent on the Sajids. 'the Sajids made the Shirvanshah Mazyadids dependent on them' (908-909 to 919, per Bakikhanov); the page does not use the word vassal.

region.text: Vaspurakan, the Artsruni kingdom on Lake Van

ledger.note: c. 909: Gagik Artsruni of Vaspurakan becomes Yusuf's vassal 'after a dispute with the Bagratids over Nakhichevan'; the page gives no year, so the start is bridged from the 909 Nakhichevan campaign.

After 917: Yusuf conquers Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray. 'After Ibn al-Furat regained the vizierate in 917, Yusuf conquered Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray from the Samanids.' The year is the vizierate's; the page does not date the conquest itself.
919: the Shirvanshah's dependence ends. The Sajids' hold over the Mazyadid Shirvanshahs lasted 'to 919' (Bakikhanov).
924: Ray reconquered. In 924 Yusuf 'conquered Ray from its governor, who had rebelled against the Samanids'. The page does not say when Ray was lost after 917.

region.text: Vaspurakan, the Artsruni kingdom on Lake Van

ledger.note: 929: the Artsruni tie lapses with the end of the dynasty (bridging; no page dates the end of Gagik's vassalage).

929: the last Sajid is poisoned and the dynasty ends. 'Fath ... was poisoned in Ardabil by one of his slaves, which ended the Sajid dynasty'; infobox 'Disestablished: 929'. The Sallarids moved 'into Azerbaijan in 941'.

wars.name: Sajid–Abbasid conflict of 908–909
wars.outcome: A caliphal army was sent in 908; al-Muqtadir made peace and invested Yusuf with Azerbaijan and Armenia in 909 for a tribute of 120 thousand dinars a year; Yusuf stopped paying after 912.

wars.name: Sajid campaigns in Armenia
wars.outcome: Nakhichevan taken in 909; Smbat's sons beaten north of Erevan in 910; Smbat trapped in a fortress about 913 and later executed; Gagik Artsruni a vassal.
wars.note: The page gives no year for Smbat's execution.

wars.name: Sajid campaign in Georgia
wars.outcome: Yusuf campaigned in Georgian territories with Tiflis as his base; no lasting hold recorded.

wars.name: Sajid conquest of Ray and its neighbours
wars.outcome: Zanjan, Abhar, Qazvin and Ray taken after 917; Ray retaken in 924.

wars.name: Sajid–Qarmatian campaign
wars.outcome: The caliph ordered Yusuf against al-Hasa in 926; his army was defeated near Kufa in 927 and he was killed in 928.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the Sajid frontiers in the Caucasus, the Araxes valley and the Ray edge are approximate.

sources.note: Yusuf's campaigns: Nakhichevan 909, Smbat, Georgia 914, Ray 917 and 924, Kufa 927.

notes: Cliopatria's Sajid row runs 898..935; the page gives 889..929, so the first nine years are added as a proxy keyframe (the 898 shape; the Caucasian conquests are undated within Muhammad's reign) and 930-935 is not drawn. The three Cliopatria shapes are nearly identical (57.9-58.2 thousand km2) and none contains the 917 Zanjan-Ray extension. No area is on either page, so the shapes could not be compared with an infobox figure. Open questions: who held Azerbaijan between 929 and the Sallarid arrival 'in 941' (the Sallarid dossier by another agent dates its gain from the Sajids to 941); the Mazyadid Shirvanshahs as dependents (908-909 to 919, Bakikhanov); the Artsruni vassalage has no year; Yusuf's Georgian campaign (914) is not a conquest. Counterparts: bagratid-armenia, kingdom-of-vaspurakan and shirvan are Cliopatria rows owned by eu-19 whose dossiers did not yet exist when this was written. Pages for the Sajid Ushrusana origin (Afshin) and the Qarmatian war were not opened (page budget 2).
